lever: batching ONLY; threads fixed at the measured winner
timing_unit: ms per invocation of B rank vectors x ALL_K_CLAIMS
layout: ranksT[nE, B] C-contiguous — eidx read once, B contiguous values

equivalence.part1: each lane vs the plain single-vector prange kernel, all k
equivalence.part2: one B=6 invocation vs six independent single invocations

winner_rule: capability winner minimises MEASURED t6, not ms/vector — a batch wider than the delta grid computes lanes that are thrown away
workload_formula: 60 worlds-needles x 999 perms x measured t6; no x6 factor, the six deltas are inside t6
excludes: per-(needle,delta,world) rank rebuilds, outer-world setup and checkpoint I/O
not_attempted: claim-order / work-balanced partitioning. The 4-thread efficiency dip (73% vs 99% at 2) looks like static-partition imbalance over claims whose nnz spans 300..83,571, but changing scheduling would be a new engine variant needing its own equivalence and benchmark.
y_status: NO Y ACCESS; all rank mappings synthetic and deterministic

baseline_correction.problem: t6_speedup_vs_B1 compares against the BATCH kernel run at B=1, which carries per-claim allocation and 2D-indexing overhead the dedicated single-vector kernel does not. That baseline flatters batching.
baseline_correction.fair_baseline_method: six sequential invocations of the plain single-vector prange kernel at the same 8 threads

anomaly_B6_slower_than_B8.note: six lanes cost MORE than eight. Consistent with SIMD width: the inner lane loop vectorises cleanly at 8 and not at 6, so computing two throwaway lanes is cheaper than losing vectorisation. Measured, not inferred from theory.
